why: The descendant half of the leaving surface's hit-testing rule, collapsed back onto the surface itself -- which is what shipped, and what read as correct because `pointer-events` is inherited. It is not enough: this file gives more than a dozen controls an explicit `pointer-events: auto`, and an explicit value on a child beats an inherited one on its parent. The mutation keeps a syntactically whole rule that still names the right property and the right value, so the brace-balance check, the no-block-inside-a-plain-rule check and the presence sweep all still pass, and `getComputedStyle` on the SURFACE still reports `none` -- only a descendant reports `auto`. Nothing about the animation, the duration or the destination moves. `takes its DESCENDANTS out of hit testing, not only itself` is the case that measures it, and it carries a negative control in the same test: the same descendant must compute `auto` while the surface is NOT leaving, so a stylesheet that disabled it unconditionally fails rather than passes. Scoped to hud.css.test.ts; expectFailures counts that scoped run only.
killedBy: a leaving surface stops eating clicks meant for the one arriving takes its DESCENDANTS out of hit testing, not only itself
